entries.german:
1347. 1. September. Krumau. — Peter vOn Rosenberg gibt dem Stifte Hohenfurt das Dorf Nesselbach nebst Zubehör zu Eigen.

LXXXVIII. Cum ad bene faciendum omnibus simus debitores, pocius tamen illis benefacere tenemur, qui nobis familiares existunt. Hinc est, quod nos Petrus de Rosenberch summus regni Bohemie camerarius et predecessores nostri monasteri i monachorum ordinis Cistarsiensis sub regula sancti Benedicti nocte dieque deuote militancium in Alto- vado fundatores existentes notum facimus vniuersis presentes per petue inspecturis, quod nos bona deliberacione maturo consilio con- sensu ac beneplacito omnium heredum nostrorum prebabito contuli- mus et exnunc assignamus et resignamus perpetue possidenda dicto monasterio in Altouado villam nostram Nesselbach cum añilura nostra atque pomerio nostro eidem ville adiacente, cum omnibus iuribus atque agris cultis et incultis pratis pascuis aquis aquarumue decur- sibus rubetis montibus planiciebus emolimentis (sic) censibus pro- uentibus aliisque cunctis vtilitatibus et pertinenciis vniuersis, que nunc ibi sunt aut fieri poterunt in futurum, quocunque nomine cen- seantur, ipsi monasterio et ad usus monachorum ibidem íleo ac beate virgini incessanter deseruiencium et sex infirmorum perpetue in hospitali sepedicti claustri connutriendorum, tali condicione adiecta, quod dictis infirmis necessaria omnia tain victus quam amictus deuo- cius ac perhenniter porrigantur consuetudinem hospitalis nostri in Chrumpnaw in omnibus obseruando, excluso dumtaxat denario, qui pro speciali recreacione singulis diebus in Chrumpnaw infirmis por- rigitur. Insuper volumus ac ordinamus et ratum perpetue habere vo- lumus, vt anniuertarius nosier in sepedicto claustro nostro singulis 89 annis post obitum nostrum sollempnius peragatur sic videlicet, vt vigilie maiores ad vesperam decantentur, et in crastino dominus ab bas, nisi legittima causa propediente missam summam celebret, reli- qui vero sacerdotes, quodquod (sic) fuerint, missas dicere eodem die non negligant pro anima nostra ac omnium predecessorum nostrorum et omnium fidelium defunctorum, vt tenentur; eodem quoque die prandium cum pitanciis in refectorio singulis laucius porrigatur, du- centis quoque pauperibus eodem die victus pro vna vice tribuatur, vnicuique vnum denarium Wyennensis vel Patauiensis monete er- rogantes, iniungendo eisdem pauperibus, vt anime nostre ac animo- rum predecessorum nostrorum et omnium fidelium defunctorum in suis oracionibus memorentur. Ceterum hortamur et rogamus, vt omnes monachi tam clerici quam layci singulis diebus in suis speci- alibus deuocionibus ob respectum diuine remuaeracionis nostri dig- nentur perpetue memorari. Hoc autem faciendum perpetue sit con- scienciis abbatis et prioris loci predicti committimus, quod si aliquid de prescriptis obmiserint, quatenus sciant, se penam qua nos ratifi- carunt incurrisse et racionem de hoc in die dei districti judicii red- dituros. Et vt prescripta robur perpetue firmitatis sorciantur, ideo iussimus presentes conscribi et eas sigilli nostri munimine roborari. Insuper ego Petrus junior de Rosenberch Pra¿ensis Olomucensis Pa tauiensis ecclesiarum cauonicus hec appensione sigilli mei ratifico ac protestor. Acta sunt hec et data in Chrumpnaw. Anno domini mille- simo trecentesimo quadragesimo septimo, ¡u die sancti Egidii con- fessoris. Zwei an Pergamentstreifen hängende Siegel. a) Ziemlich gross und in weissem Wachs abgedruckt. Ein Ritter hoch'zu Hoss, das mit einer rosenbe- säeten Schabracke bedeckt ist und am Halse und Hinterschenkeln Schilde mit fünfblättrigen Rosen trägt, schwingt in seiner Rechten ein Schwert und hält in der Linken einen Schild mit einer Rose zum Abzeichen; gleichfalls aus einer Rose besteht die Zierde des Helmes und die Kopfzierdc des Pferdes. — Si- gillvm . entries.english:
1347, 1 September, Krumau. — Peter von Rosenberg grants the village of Nesselbach and its appurtenances in free ownership to Hohenfurt Monastery.

Since we are obliged to do good to everyone, we are especially bound to do good to those who are close to us. Therefore we, Peter von Rosenberg, supreme chamberlain of the kingdom of Bohemia, founder, together with our predecessors, of the monastery of monks of the Cistercian Order at Hohenfurt, who serve God and the Blessed Virgin devoutly day and night under the Rule of Saint Benedict, make known to all who will forever see this document that, after due deliberation, mature counsel, and the consent and approval of all our heirs, we have granted and from this time assign and surrender in perpetuity to the aforesaid monastery at Hohenfurt our village of Nesselbach, together with our mill and orchard adjoining the village, with all rights, cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, thickets, mountains, plains, revenues, rents, income, and every other utility and appurtenance now there or that may arise in future, by whatever name they are called. These are for the monastery and for the use of the monks serving God and the Blessed Virgin there without ceasing, and for the perpetual maintenance of six sick people in the hospital of the aforesaid monastery. The condition is that all necessities, both food and clothing, be provided generously and perpetually to those sick people, observing in all respects the custom of our hospital at Krumau, except only the penny given each day at Krumau to the sick for their special refreshment.

Furthermore, we wish and decree, and desire to have it forever observed, that our anniversary be solemnly celebrated in the aforesaid monastery each year after our death: the greater vigils are to be sung in the evening; on the following day the abbot, unless prevented by a legitimate cause, is to celebrate High Mass, and all the other priests, however many there may be, are not to neglect to say Masses that day for our soul, the souls of all our predecessors, and all the faithful departed, as they are bound to do. On that day, a meal with generous portions is also to be served to each in the refectory, and food for one meal is to be given to two hundred poor people, with one penny of Viennese or Passau currency distributed to each. They are to be charged to remember our soul, the souls of our predecessors, and all the faithful departed in their prayers. We also exhort and ask all monks, clergy and lay brothers, to remember us perpetually every day in their private devotions, for the sake of divine reward. We entrust the perpetual observance of this to the consciences of the abbot and prior of the aforesaid place, so that if they omit anything prescribed, they may know that they incur the penalty they have acknowledged and will answer for it on the day of God's strict judgment. To give the foregoing perpetual force, we have ordered this document to be written and strengthened with the protection of our seal.

I, Peter the Younger von Rosenberg, canon of the churches of Prague, Olomouc, and Passau, confirm and attest this by appending my seal. Done and issued at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1347, on the day of Saint Giles the Confessor.

Two seals hang from parchment strips. (a) Rather large, impressed in white wax: a knight on horseback, with a rose-covered saddlecloth and shields bearing five-petalled roses at the horse's neck and hindquarters, swings a sword in his right hand and holds in his left a shield bearing a rose; a rose also forms the crest of the helmet and the horse's head. — Seal of Peter von Rosenberg. The counterseal is in red wax, as in no. LXXXII. (b) A seal the size of a thaler, in white wax: a figure in a long flowing robe, with a kind of halo around the head, holds a shield bearing a rose before him in his right hand; another such shield is at the right side of the seal. — Seal of Peter von Rosenberg, canon of Prague.
